column1: # #404 — the arms of the card, one row each. Tab separated.
# Columns: arm, α at step 0, α at the end of the ramp, the ramp length, the
# backbone seed. A `-` in a column is a flag the arm does NOT pass.
# Only α and the seed change. Every other flag of every arm comes from #373's
# cell `arm6_v2_combab_alignT` at k = 32, under the mean reduction.
# The card says to add arms if the four scores show a direction — a value
# between two good values, or a smaller fixed value. Add a row here and
# nothing else changes: every script, guard and figure reads this file.
# Rows 1 to 4 are the card's own four arms. Rows 5 and 6 answer the review of
#   a095  above 0.9. The fixed row falls 0.0490 from 0.8 to 0.9 and does not
#         turn, so the next value belongs above 0.9 and not inside that
#         segment.
#   s08b  s08 again at a second backbone seed. It measures THIS cell's repeat
#         spread. Before it, the card quoted #373's spread, which was measured
#         at k = 3 against the student target.
# Rows 7 and 8 answer what `s08b` then showed. `s08b` did not measure noise:
# its backbone FELL TO CHANCE while it trained. Its contrastive AUC went 0.91
# at 10,000 steps to 0.57 at 40,000, its top1 went 0.273 to 0.009, and it
# scored 1.5459 against s08's 1.1782. Every other arm holds AUC 0.93 to 0.98,
# and every one of those five carries backbone seed 20260520. So one seed
# collapsed and one seed did not, and two readings fit that:
#   - 20260521 was unlucky, and a collapse in this cell is rare, or
#   - 20260520 was lucky, and this cell is unstable.
# Under the second reading every ranking of this card rests on one seed. Two
# more seeds of the SAME arm tell the two apart:
#   s08c  s08 at backbone seed 20260522
#   s08d  s08 at backbone seed 20260523
# `a085` was planned and then DROPPED. Alpha 0.85 interpolates inside the
# 0.8-to-0.9 segment, and that segment already falls in one direction. The
# value above 0.9 buys more.
# 20260521 is the project's second backbone seed. #373 measured its own seed
# band with it (cell B5·s2), so this repeat stays in that family. 20260522 and
# 20260523 continue that count.
# Rows 9 and 10 turn the card back to the SCORE. The card wants a lower
# GM-Relative MASE. Rows 7 and 8 measure the collapse rate, and no arm of this
# card beats the k = 0 parent at 1.1600. The best arm here holds 1.1782.
# The RAMP LENGTH is the one axis this card never moved. Every ramp arm of
# rows 1 to 8 runs 200,000 steps. The EMA schedule ladder,
# reports/2026-08-04_ema_sched_ladder/, trained ten runs on that axis. A
# momentum that reaches 1.0 at step 100,000 scored 0.0259 BELOW the fixed 0.9
# reference at the 40,000-step stop, where the momentum held 0.94. The same run
# scored 0.0251 ABOVE at the 100,000-step stop, where the momentum held 1.0.
# The ladder's latent table gives the reason: past step 100,000 the teacher
# latent moves 0.019 or less per 20,000 steps, so a momentum at 1.0 freezes the
# teacher.
#   r100_09  0.9 to 1.0 over 100,000 steps. It holds 0.940 at the stop, which
#            is the value the ladder measured as its best.
#   r100_08  0.8 to 1.0 over 100,000 steps. It holds 0.880 at the stop, and
#            brackets r100_09 from below.
# The two 200,000-step ramps hold 0.840 and 0.920 at the stop, so the four
# ramp arms give one ordered row: 0.840, 0.880, 0.920, 0.940. Neither new arm
# reaches 1.0 at the stop, so neither freezes its teacher there.
# Both new arms carry backbone seed 20260520, the seed of the six scored arms.
# A new seed here would move two values at once.
# arm
s08b
s08c
s08d
